correctness.rationale: Direct solution of both ODE segments gives the stated two-exponential formula. The original sag is strictly unimodal. For candidate locations before its peak, the upstream worst deficit increases strictly while the downstream worst deficit decreases strictly, yielding a single global minimizer. The full-peak equality has exactly one solution and gives an exact reach-length saturation threshold. Differentiation of the finite-reach crossing equation proves monotonicity, first-order expansion proves the short-reach limit, and exact downstream-peak curvature -ab times its peak height proves the quadratic contact coefficient; endpoint and critical-length regimes are explicitly verified. CHECK.py uses finite numerical cross-checks without claiming they prove global optimality.

originality.rationale: The claim is confined to a single fixed-fraction deficit reset under a finite-reach maximum-deficit objective, including an explicit threshold and quadratic approach-to-plateau coefficient. The full inspected Rinaldi--Soncini-Sessa analysis instead minimizes aerator cost subject to oxygen-standard constraints and leaves device number/power as controls; its Property A supplies a relevant qualitative placement principle, but not this exact finite-horizon theorem or coefficient. The foundational Streeter--Phelps model is acknowledged. The Koivo--Phillips 1975 in-stream aeration paper could not be inspected in full, and broad minimax control results may cover the narrow result; those are recorded as genuine residual risk, not ruled out by search absence.
residual_risks: Koivo--Phillips (1975) full text could not be read, despite title directly concerning oxygen optimization with in-stream aeration; it could contain an exactly equivalent specialized theorem.

A general L-infinity impulse-control result or minimax design principle might imply this finite-reach single-fixed-fraction classification and quadratic plateau; no exhaustive novelty proof is possible.

value.rationale: A finite downstream reach, one device, and an efficiency fixed by local deficit are motivated engineering constraints distinct from arbitrary device-placement slices. The solved quantity is the unique minimizer of worst oxygen deficit across an entire continuous reach, not a trivial endpoint check. The critical length separating endpoint-limited and interior-peak-limited design, the exact location equation and a sharp second-order placement saturation coefficient answer meaningful sensitivity questions with plausible future use in calibrated simplified aerator-placement studies. This is not claimed as a full water-quality engineering design or a new theory of minimizing maxima.
